kb_editor_cancel.label: Escape: Finish linking, cancel a pending paste, or drop the selection

kb_editor_cursor.label: Canvas focused: arrow keys move the cursor, Space or Enter paints with the active tool

kb_editor_select.label: S: Select tool. Drag or Shift+arrows select a rectangle; Ctrl (Cmd) + C / X / V copy, cut, paste; Delete clears; Shift+F fills the selection with the chosen palette entry; Alt+arrows or dragging inside the selection move it; Escape cancels a paste or drops the selection

kb_editor_history.label: Ctrl+Z / Ctrl+Y: Undo / Redo | Ctrl+S: Save

cc3d_machine.label: Needs a clone machine: this switch works nothing yet.

cc3d_template.label: Needs a creature or block standing on it: a clone machine copies what stands on it, and this one has nothing to copy.

cc3d_shooter.label: Needs a laser shooter: this controller fires nothing yet.

cc3d_toggle_door.label: Needs a toggle control of the same colour ({colour}): nothing flips this door yet.

lynx.label: Lynx levels: only trap and clone links exist, one per button; a brown or red button with no link does nothing, and its trap or clone machine stays shut.

trap.name: Trap control and trap
trap.label: A trap control opens the next trap after it in reading order, or the first trap when none follows. A trap is open while any control that works it is pressed; a trap no control works stays closed.

teleport.name: Red and blue teleports
teleport.label: A teleport sends to the previous teleport of its colour in reading order, and the first one sends to the last. A teleport that is occupied, or whose exits are blocked, is skipped for the one before it; a lone teleport goes nowhere.

clone.name: Clone switch, machine and template
clone.label: A clone switch works the nearest clone machine (on a tie, the first in reading order). The creature or block standing on a machine is its template. When the switch is pressed, the template leaves the way the machine faces, or its own facing on a machine with no direction, and a copy takes its place. If its way out is blocked, nothing happens.

laser.name: Laser controller and shooter
laser.label: A laser controller fires the nearest laser shooter (on a tie, the first in reading order) once each time something that works switches steps onto it. With no shooter it fires nothing.

toggle.name: Toggle control and door
toggle.label: Each time something that works switches steps onto a toggle control, every toggle door of its colour flips between open and closed; leaving changes nothing. A control with no door of its colour flips nothing.

hold.name: Plate and hold door
hold.label: A hold door of a colour is open only while every plate of its colour is pressed. A colour with no plates keeps its doors closed.

golem_blue.name: Blue golem control and golems
golem_blue.label: Each time something that works switches starts a step onto a blue golem control, every blue golem turns around.

golem_yellow.name: Yellow golem control and golems
golem_yellow.label: Each time the player steps onto a yellow golem control, every yellow golem tries to take one step in the direction the player was moving. Only the player works it.

top_layer.label: Toggle controls, clone switches, laser controllers, golem controls and teleports work only from the top layer of their cell; plates and trap controls work from any layer.

block_color_red.label: Colour block pushing rules differ slightly from CC3D, and a floating block cannot be pushed again.

block_color_green.name: Colour block (green)
block_color_green.label: Colour block pushing rules differ slightly from CC3D, and a floating block cannot be pushed again.

block_color_blue.name: Colour block (blue)
block_color_blue.label: Colour block pushing rules differ slightly from CC3D, and a floating block cannot be pushed again.

block_color_yellow.name: Colour block (yellow)
block_color_yellow.label: Colour block pushing rules differ slightly from CC3D, and a floating block cannot be pushed again.

reflector.name: Reflector
reflector.label: Epoxy plays a reflector as a one-sided mirror: it turns shots and beams from its two reflecting faces and destroys a shot coming from behind. Mirrors are turned to match their reflecting faces. Bounce timing differs from CC3D.

walker.name: Walker
walker.label: Monster movement is close to CC3D, not identical.

legs_green.name: Green legs
legs_green.label: Epoxy plays the green legs as a fireball, which is immune to fire where the legs are not. The legs' pattern switching is not reproduced. Unlike the CC3D legs, it does not press plates.

legs_red.name: Red legs
legs_red.label: Epoxy plays the red legs as a glider, which is immune to water where the legs are not. The legs' pattern switching is not reproduced. Unlike the CC3D legs, it does not press plates.

blinky.name: Blinky
blinky.label: Monster movement is close to CC3D, not identical.

baby_blinky.name: Baby blinky
baby_blinky.label: Monster movement is close to CC3D, not identical. Unlike the CC3D one, it does not press plates.

limpa.name: Limpa
limpa.label: Monster movement is close to CC3D, not identical.

limpy.name: Limpy
limpy.label: Monster movement is close to CC3D, not identical.

bouncer.name: Bouncer
bouncer.label: Monster movement is close to CC3D, not identical.

omni.name: Omni
omni.label: Monster movement is close to CC3D, not identical.

screamer.name: Screamer
screamer.label: Epoxy plays the screamer as a fireball, which is immune to fire but not to ice and force floors, which the screamer ignores. The screamer melting ice blocks is not reproduced.

baby_screamer.name: Baby screamer
baby_screamer.label: Epoxy plays the baby screamer as a fireball: the immunity to fire matches, but it does not melt ice blocks and, unlike the CC3D one, does not press plates.

snappy.name: Snappy
snappy.label: Monster movement is close to CC3D, not identical.

bot_static.name: Static bot
bot_static.label: Epoxy plays a bot as a turret: the beam and its turn period are close to CC3D, with a beam length and a period that are guesses, and Epoxy makes no turn at the first step.

bot_cw.name: Clockwise bot
bot_cw.label: Epoxy plays a bot as a turret: the beam and its turn period are close to CC3D, with a beam length and a period that are guesses, and Epoxy makes no turn at the first step.

bot_ccw.name: Counter-clockwise bot
bot_ccw.label: Epoxy plays a bot as a turret: the beam and its turn period are close to CC3D, with a beam length and a period that are guesses, and Epoxy makes no turn at the first step.

bot_multi.name: Multi-turn bot
bot_multi.label: Epoxy plays a bot as a turret: the beam and its turn period are close to CC3D, with a beam length and a period that are guesses, and Epoxy makes no turn at the first step.

golem_yellow.name: Yellow golem
golem_yellow.label: Epoxy plays the yellow golem as a puppet that steps at once when the player ends a move on the control, where CC3D walks it one step. It can enter Epoxy gravel, which stands for both CC3D sand (the golem enters it) and CC3D gravel (the golem is stopped by it). The order of entry along a line of puppets differs.

golem_control_yellow.name: Yellow golem control
golem_control_yellow.label: Epoxy plays the yellow golem control as the puppet control: only the player works it, and a puppet or block entering it does nothing, as in CC3D. The order of the steps differs.

nibble.name: Nibble
nibble.label: Epoxy plays a nibble as a skitter: it steps away from the player along the axis of the greater distance, at a fixed step interval.

golem_blue.name: Blue golem
golem_blue.label: Golem movement is close to CC3D, not identical.

laser_controller.name: Laser controller
laser_controller.label: Epoxy plays the laser controller as a shot trigger linked to the shooters it fires (CC3D uses the nearest shooter). In CC3D any monster works it; in Epoxy anything that steps on it does. A trigger hidden under a removable top acts only once revealed.

laser_shooter.name: Laser shooter
laser_shooter.label: Epoxy plays the shooter as a shot launcher: a wall-like tile that fires the way it faces, so the terrain under the shooter is flattened. A shot crosses cells at the CC3D pace, but its opacity follows Epoxy laser transparency, and the exit and the first cell hit can differ.

trap_unworked.name: Trap without a control
trap_unworked.label: No trap control works this trap: CC3D keeps it shut, where Epoxy opens an unlinked trap with any brown button.

clone_switch_empty.name: Clone switch with nothing to clone
clone_switch_empty.label: The nearest clone machine of this switch holds no template Epoxy can clone (none, or a laser shooter): CC3D does nothing, and a switch left unlinked would fire every machine in Epoxy, so the converter drops the switch link.

bomb_with_item.name: Bomb sharing a cell with an item
bomb_with_item.label: A bomb layer shares its cell with an item: Epoxy holds one item per cell, so the bomb is dropped and the item stays.

laser_shooter_covered.name: Laser shooter on an item or another layer
laser_shooter_covered.label: The shooter stands on an item or on a layer other than plain floor (a device, a machine, ground): the Epoxy launcher replaces the whole cell, so what was there is dropped, and a shooter used as a clone template is not cloned.

stacked_runtime.name: Stack that acts while covered
stacked_runtime.label: The stack has a layer that acts while covered under a top that is not a door or a socket, or more layers than a removable top and the one it hides, which Epoxy flattens.

hold_door_red.name: Hold door (red)
hold_door_red.label: Epoxy plays the hold door as CC3D does: all plates of its colour, occupant may leave, nobody may enter.

hold_door_green.name: Hold door (green)
hold_door_green.label: Epoxy plays the hold door as CC3D does: all plates of its colour, occupant may leave, nobody may enter.

hold_door_blue.name: Hold door (blue)
hold_door_blue.label: Epoxy plays the hold door as CC3D does: all plates of its colour, occupant may leave, nobody may enter.

hold_door_yellow.name: Hold door (yellow)
hold_door_yellow.label: Epoxy plays the hold door as CC3D does: all plates of its colour, occupant may leave, nobody may enter.

desc.label: Blocks its north and east sides. After something passes through, it turns a quarter turn so the side it came in by closes.
Blocks its south and east sides. After something passes through, it turns a quarter turn so the side it came in by closes.
Blocks its south and west sides. After something passes through, it turns a quarter turn so the side it came in by closes.
Blocks its north and west sides. After something passes through, it turns a quarter turn so the side it came in by closes.
Swaps a monster that arrives on it for its paired kind (bug and paramecium, glider and fireball, teeth and skitter, pink ball and walker).
Turns an arrow block that arrives on it a quarter turn clockwise, arrows included. Only arrow blocks turn: monsters and the player are not affected.
Turns an arrow block that arrives on it a quarter turn counter-clockwise, arrows included. Only arrow blocks turn: monsters and the player are not affected.
While held, the player walks twice as fast.
While held, hidden walls (invisible and appearing walls) are revealed.
While held, stepping away from a resting block pulls it behind you.
While held, every monster takes twice as long per step. A thief takes it.
Flips every plain toggle wall between closed and open. Needs: toggle walls (not the coloured ones, which have their own toggle buttons).
Makes every tank turn round. Needs: tanks.
Opens traps while held. Link it to traps with K or Link...; a trap that no link names opens with any brown button.
A spot to cover with a block. Needs: the win rule that asks to cover every target.
Fires clone machines. Link it to machines with K or Link...; with no link, it fires every clone machine that holds a creature.
Turns every flame jet on or off. Needs: flame jets.
Swaps the chips and bombs within two cells of it (a 5 x 5 area).
Harmless while off. An orange button turns it on. Needs: an orange button.
Burns the player unless they wear fire boots; only fire-proof monsters enter it, and lighting it kills monsters on it and melts ice blocks. An orange button turns it off. Needs: an orange button.
A wall until a green button is pressed, then it opens. Needs: a green button.
Open floor until a green button is pressed, then it closes. Needs: a green button.
Sends whatever enters it to the previous plain teleporter in reading order, wrapping round; it skips ones whose exit is blocked. Needs: a second teleporter.
Chains only with red teleporters. Needs: another red teleporter.
Chains only with blue teleporters. Needs: another blue teleporter.
Chains only with yellow teleporters. Needs: another yellow teleporter.
Chains only with green teleporters. Needs: another green teleporter.
Holds whatever steps in until a brown button is held. Needs: a brown button (link it with K or Link...; a trap that no link names stays open while any brown button is held down).
Copies the monster or block on it, turrets included, into the cell it faces when its red button is pressed. Needs: a red button, and a creature on the machine.
Casts a straight beam to the north that kills the player and monsters. Mirrors turn it 90 degrees; walls stop it.
Casts a straight beam to the east that kills the player and monsters. Mirrors turn it 90 degrees; walls stop it.
Casts a straight beam to the south that kills the player and monsters. Mirrors turn it 90 degrees; walls stop it.
Casts a straight beam to the west that kills the player and monsters. Mirrors turn it 90 degrees; walls stop it.
Holds the red laser gates open while a beam lights it. Needs: a laser emitter, and red laser gates.
Holds the blue laser gates open while a beam lights it. Needs: a laser emitter, and blue laser gates.
Open while a red laser receiver is lit, closed otherwise. Needs: a red laser receiver.
Open while a red laser receiver is lit, closed otherwise. Needs: a red laser receiver.
Open while a blue laser receiver is lit, closed otherwise. Needs: a blue laser receiver.
Open while a blue laser receiver is lit, closed otherwise. Needs: a blue laser receiver.
A red hold door stays open while every red plate is pressed. Needs: a red hold door.
A green hold door stays open while every green plate is pressed. Needs: a green hold door.
A blue hold door stays open while every blue plate is pressed. Needs: a blue hold door.
A yellow hold door stays open while every yellow plate is pressed. Needs: a yellow hold door.
Sends a signal while something stands on it. Needs: a signal link to a gate or a hold door.
Sends a signal while every linked input is sending one. Needs: signal links in and out.
Sends a signal while any linked input is sending one. Needs: signal links in and out.
Sends a signal while its one linked input is not sending one. Needs: one signal link in, and one out.
Sends a signal while an odd number of its linked inputs are sending one. Needs: signal links in and out.
Flips between sending and not sending each time its input starts sending; starts off. Needs: signal links in and out.
Flips between sending and not sending each time its input starts sending; starts on. Needs: signal links in and out.
Opens while something stands on every pressure plate of its colour. Needs: a red pressure plate (without one it stays shut).
Open while something stands on every pressure plate of its colour. Needs: a red pressure plate (without one it stays shut).
Opens while something stands on every pressure plate of its colour. Needs: a green pressure plate (without one it stays shut).
Open while something stands on every pressure plate of its colour. Needs: a green pressure plate (without one it stays shut).
Opens while something stands on every pressure plate of its colour. Needs: a blue pressure plate (without one it stays shut).
Open while something stands on every pressure plate of its colour. Needs: a blue pressure plate (without one it stays shut).
Opens while something stands on every pressure plate of its colour. Needs: a yellow pressure plate (without one it stays shut).
Open while something stands on every pressure plate of its colour. Needs: a yellow pressure plate (without one it stays shut).
A wall until a red toggle button is pressed, then it opens. Needs: a red toggle button.
Open floor until a red toggle button is pressed, then it closes. Needs: a red toggle button.
A wall until a blue toggle button is pressed, then it opens. Needs: a blue toggle button.
Open floor until a blue toggle button is pressed, then it closes. Needs: a blue toggle button.
A wall until a yellow toggle button is pressed, then it opens. Needs: a yellow toggle button.
Open floor until a yellow toggle button is pressed, then it closes. Needs: a yellow toggle button.
Flips every red toggle wall between closed and open. Needs: red toggle walls.
Flips every blue toggle wall between closed and open. Needs: blue toggle walls.
Flips every yellow toggle wall between closed and open. Needs: yellow toggle walls.
When the player ends a move on it, every puppet steps one cell the same way the player moved, pushing a block if one is in the way. Needs: puppets.

Fires a shot to the north when a shot trigger linked to it is pressed. A shot kills the player, monsters and turrets, melts ice blocks, sets off bombs and turns off mirrors; walls, other blocks and items stop it. Needs: a shot trigger linked with K or Link...

Fires a shot to the east when a shot trigger linked to it is pressed. A shot kills the player, monsters and turrets, melts ice blocks, sets off bombs and turns off mirrors; walls, other blocks and items stop it. Needs: a shot trigger linked with K or Link...

Fires a shot to the south when a shot trigger linked to it is pressed. A shot kills the player, monsters and turrets, melts ice blocks, sets off bombs and turns off mirrors; walls, other blocks and items stop it. Needs: a shot trigger linked with K or Link...

Fires a shot to the west when a shot trigger linked to it is pressed. A shot kills the player, monsters and turrets, melts ice blocks, sets off bombs and turns off mirrors; walls, other blocks and items stop it. Needs: a shot trigger linked with K or Link...
Fires its linked launchers. Needs: launchers linked with K or Link... (unlinked, it fires nothing).
Walkable, like floor. It is what a red colour block becomes when it is pushed into water.
Walkable, like floor. It is what a green colour block becomes when it is pushed into water.
Walkable, like floor. It is what a blue colour block becomes when it is pushed into water.
Walkable, like floor. It is what a yellow colour block becomes when it is pushed into water.
A block the player can push. Pushed into water, it turns the water into dirt.
A pushable block that moves only toward the one side that shows an arrow. Pushed from any other side, it stays still.
A pushable block that moves only toward the two opposite sides that show an arrow. Pushed from any other side, it stays still.
A pushable block that moves only toward the two adjacent sides that show an arrow. Pushed from any other side, it stays still.
A pushable block that moves only toward the three sides that show an arrow. Pushed from the fourth side, it stays still.
A block the player can push. Melts into water in fire; a shot also destroys it, leaving water only on plain floor.
A creature that does not move on its own: it steps only when the player works a puppet control. It presses plates and pushes blocks. Needs: a puppet control.
Runs from the player, first along the axis where it is farther away (sideways on a tie), then the other; when lined up it backs straight away.
A pushable block that fires a 3-cell beam in the way it faces, killing the first player or monster it reaches. It never turns.
A pushable block that fires a 3-cell beam, killing the first player or monster it reaches. It turns clockwise every 60 ticks.
A pushable block that fires a 3-cell beam, killing the first player or monster it reaches. It turns counter-clockwise every 60 ticks.
A pushable block that fires a 3-cell beam on all four sides, killing the first player or monster each beam reaches.
A pushable mirror that turns a laser beam or a shot 90 degrees. It refuses water.
A pushable mirror that turns a laser beam or a shot 90 degrees. It refuses water.
A pushable mirror that turns a beam or a shot only on its north-east face; a shot from behind destroys it; a laser beam from behind just stops on it. It refuses water.
A pushable mirror that turns a beam or a shot only on its north-west face; a shot from behind destroys it; a laser beam from behind just stops on it. It refuses water.
A pushable mirror that turns a beam or a shot only on its south-east face; a shot from behind destroys it; a laser beam from behind just stops on it. It refuses water.
A pushable mirror that turns a beam or a shot only on its south-west face; a shot from behind destroys it; a laser beam from behind just stops on it. It refuses water.
A pushable block that presses only the red pressure plates (other blocks and the player press any). Pushed into water, it floats as a walkable block.
A pushable block that presses only the green pressure plates (other blocks and the player press any). Pushed into water, it floats as a walkable block.
A pushable block that presses only the blue pressure plates (other blocks and the player press any). Pushed into water, it floats as a walkable block.
A pushable block that presses only the yellow pressure plates (other blocks and the player press any). Pushed into water, it floats as a walkable block.

level_1.title: Power Up
level_1.hint: Collect every chip to open the socket, then step through the exit.

level_2.title: Color Codes
level_2.hint: A key opens the door of its color and is used up. Green keys stay in your pocket.

level_3.title: Landfill
level_3.hint: Push a block into water to make dirt you can walk over. Blocks cannot cross dirt, so walk on it first. The wide channel needs two blocks in the same row.

level_4.title: Dress Code
level_4.hint: Flippers carry you across water, fire boots through flames. Find them in the right order.

level_5.title: Black Ice
level_5.hint: On ice you slide until you reach solid ground. Curved corners turn your slide.

level_6.title: One Way Ticket
level_6.hint: Conveyors only run one way. Force boots let you walk against them.

level_7.title: Airlock
level_7.hint: A green button flips every toggle wall. A wall that closes behind you opens again at the next press.

level_8.title: Hold the Line
level_8.hint: A trap holds whatever enters it while its brown button is free. Park a block on the button first.

level_9.title: Blast Radius
level_9.hint: A block pushed into a bomb destroys both. Count the bombs before you spend a block: one is needed for the water.

level_10.title: Relay
level_10.hint: A pad sends you to the pad of the same color, still moving the same way. The side you enter from decides where you land.

level_11.title: Allotments
level_11.hint: Thin fences stop you and blocks on one edge only. Blocks cannot cross dirt: walk on it first to clear the way.

level_12.title: Workshop
level_12.hint: Every wing holds a key or a chip. The conveyor out of the east wing runs one way, and the green button where it ends opens the way back.

level_13.title: Night Shift
level_13.hint: Bugs keep a wall on their left and never step on gravel or on an item. Wait in a gravel nook, then move when the way is clear.

level_14.title: Ricochet
level_14.hint: Balls roll straight and bounce back off anything, chips included. Take a chip and its lane grows longer.

level_15.title: Reverse Gear
level_15.hint: Tanks drive straight until something stops them. The blue button turns every tank around: stand clear of their tracks when you press it, and never wait in the bay at the bottom.

level_16.title: Mirage
level_16.hint: Some blue walls melt when you walk into them, others hold. Below, invisible walls appear only when you bump into them.

level_17.title: Assembly Line
level_17.hint: Each press of the red button makes a new block in the machine. Blocks are free: if one gets stuck, make another.

level_18.title: Dash
level_18.hint: Teeth chase you but move slower than you. The clock is tight: plan your loop around the pillars before you start.

level_19.title: Pickpocket
level_19.hint: The thief takes every pair of boots you carry. Look for a way past him before you need your boots again.

level_20.title: Customs
level_20.hint: A barrier stops you while you carry the item it shows. Spend the key first, and let the thief lighten your load.

level_21.title: Light Fingers
level_21.hint: This thief takes every key you carry, green ones too. Open what you can before you cross him, and find another way back.

level_22.title: Stepping Stones
level_22.hint: A turtle carries you across the water once, then dives. Each turtle bridge works one way only: choose the first one with care.

level_23.title: Hot Swap
level_23.hint: The orange button switches every flame jet: lit ones go out, cold ones light up. Check the next row before you press.

level_24.title: Contraband
level_24.hint: Turtles, flames and a customs barrier. A turtle you step back from is gone, so cross in one go. Spend the red key before you head for the exit.

level_25.title: Spending Spree
level_25.hint: Two blue keys, three blue doors. Look into every wing before you open one: only one order reaches the yellow key.

level_26.title: Cold Storage
level_26.hint: Blocks slide on ice and turn at curved corners, just like you. Follow each block path to the water before you push.

level_27.title: Countdown
level_27.hint: Two teeth hunt you and the clock is short. Stopwatches add ten seconds: grab them on the way.

level_28.title: Hideouts
level_28.hint: Creatures cannot cross blue walls, but a blue wall you walk through is gone for good. Once a hideout is open, they can follow you in.

level_29.title: Open Air
level_29.hint: Gliders circle the edge of the plaza. Each wing gives the key to the next one: red, then blue, then yellow. In the west wing, park a block on the brown button before you step on the trap.

level_30.title: Epoxy Core
level_30.hint: Everything you learned, one wing at a time. The green key opens both green doors, but the thief at the east wing takes it: open them before you go there.

keys_doors.title: Locksmith Run #{number}
keys_doors.hint: Each colored door eats a key of its color. Green keys open every green door.

fire.title: Ember Crossing #{number}
fire.hint: Fire burns without fire boots. Look for them before you step in.

water.title: Flooded Halls #{number}
water.hint: Water drowns you without flippers. Grab them first.

blocks_water.title: Bridge Builders #{number}
blocks_water.hint: Push a block into water to turn it into dirt you can walk on. Plan the push before you move.

ice.title: Glacier Drift #{number}
ice.hint: Ice keeps you sliding until something stops you. Corners turn your slide.

force.title: Conveyor Works #{number}
force.hint: Force floors carry you along. Force boots let you walk against them.

thief.title: Thieves' Den #{number}
thief.hint: The thief takes all your boots. Use them before you meet him.

toggle_walls.title: Switchyard #{number}
toggle_walls.hint: Every green button flips every toggle wall. Count your presses.

trap.title: Bear Trap Alley #{number}
trap.hint: A bear trap holds you until its brown button is pressed. A block can keep the button down.

teleport.title: Quantum Hop #{number}
teleport.hint: Step on a teleporter to come out of another one, moving the same way. With several pads, the order you use them matters.

sokoban.title: Warehouse #{number}
sokoban.hint: Every brown button holds a trap open. Push a block onto each button, and never into a corner.

monsters.title: Creature Feature #{number}
monsters.hint: Monsters follow fixed patterns. Watch them, wait for the gap, then move.

bomb.title: Demolition Run #{number}
bomb.hint: Bombs blow up anything that touches them. Push a block into one to clear the way.

cloner.title: Clone Works #{number}
cloner.hint: A red button makes the clone machine drop a copy of its block. Clone as many blocks as the job needs.

dirt.title: Excavation #{number}
dirt.hint: Blocks cannot cross dirt or fake blue walls until you clear them on foot. Clear the right path before you push.

default.hint: Use the Objective button (or H) to locate the next mechanism and inspect trap, cloner, and toggle links.

1.title: Foundations
1.subtitle: Chips, keys, boots, ice and force floors.

2.title: Mechanisms
2.subtitle: Buttons, traps, bombs, teleporters and thin walls.

3.title: Creatures
3.subtitle: Bugs, tanks, hidden walls and clone machines.

4.title: Contraband
4.subtitle: Thieves, item barriers, turtles and flame jets.

5.title: Core
5.subtitle: Gold keys, bonus clocks and fast hunters, all together.

level_1.title: Power Up
level_1.hint: Collect every chip to open the socket, then step through the exit.

level_2.title: Four Pens
level_2.hint: A thin wall closes only one edge of a square, so check which side of each pen is open before you walk in.

level_3.title: Two Doors, Two Keys
level_3.hint: A red key opens one red door and then disappears, so spend each key on the door right after it.

level_4.title: The Two Attics
level_4.hint: Think before you open a door, and if you get stuck press U to undo a step or R to restart.

level_5.title: The Greenhouse Keeper
level_5.hint: A green key is never used up: one key opens every green door.

level_6.title: Footprints
level_6.hint: Dirt turns into floor once you step on it, so the dirt that is left shows where you have not been yet.

level_7.title: Printed Circuit
level_7.hint: The socket opens when its counter reaches zero.

level_8.title: The Cheapest Basket
level_8.hint: The counter shows how many chips the socket still needs, not how many lie on the board, so you do not have to take them all.

level_9.title: The Socket Door
level_9.hint: The socket is not always the last gate: look at what lies behind it before you count on the exit.

level_10.title: The Key Ring
level_10.hint: A red door eats the key that opens it: count keys before opening a room without one.

level_11.title: The Hedge
level_11.hint: A key you keep is worth more than the steps you save.

level_12.title: The Orchard
level_12.hint: The socket asks for six chips, not all nine: work out which rooms you really need before a red key opens one.

level_13.title: Zen Garden
level_13.hint: Nothing in this garden can lock you out, so take the chips in any order and enjoy the walk.

level_14.title: Two Key Rings
level_14.hint: A key can hide behind a door of the other colour: trace the chain backwards to find the one lock everything else hangs from.

level_15.title: The Clockmaker
level_15.hint: A spent key is gone for good: before opening a door, check that the keys still out of reach can pay for what remains.

level_16.title: The Bends
level_16.hint: Walking into a block pushes it one cell, so slide each block into a free cell beside your way to clear the corridor.

level_17.title: The Ford
level_17.hint: Water drowns you, but a block pushed into it fills the pool.

level_18.title: The Rails
level_18.hint: Cover every target with a block to win, there is no exit, and a block only moves straight ahead of you.

level_19.title: Dead Ends
level_19.hint: Before you push, look where the block will stop: in a corner, along a wall with no target or squeezed in a square, it can never move again.

level_20.title: The Trodden Bridge
level_20.hint: A two-wide river needs two blocks in the same row, and fresh dirt stops a block until you have walked over it.

level_21.title: The Embankment
level_21.hint: A block sunk in the river leaves a bridge, but a bridge only helps a block that travels in the row of its target.

level_22.title: Tidying Up
level_22.hint: Every block lies a few pushes from its target: cover all the targets to win, in whatever order you like.

level_23.title: The Metronome
level_23.hint: A pink ball runs straight along its corridor and turns back at a wall, and a block stops it: it can neither cross one nor push it.

level_24.title: The Crossing
level_24.hint: A pink ball never steps on gravel, and a block between you and the ball keeps it away from you.

level_25.title: The Workshop
level_25.hint: A block that stops above an empty target is stuck for good once another block rests on it, so fill a bay from the bottom.

level_26.title: The Doorkeeper
level_26.hint: A key opens one door and is spent, a block cannot pass a closed door, and fresh dirt stops a block until you have walked on it.

level_27.title: Don't Dig
level_27.hint: A pink ball runs straight until something stops it, and dirt stops it. Walk through that dirt and the ball runs on.

level_28.title: Four Splashes
level_28.hint: A block pushed into water sinks and leaves dirt you can walk on: one block, one pool.

level_29.title: The Lock
level_29.hint: Every pool and every pink ball you must stop costs one block, and a block spent on another job is gone. A pink ball cannot pass a block.

level_30.title: The Great Works
level_30.hint: Cover every target to win. A block fills a pool or covers a target, never both. A block on the top or bottom row can never leave it, so send each of those rows exactly two blocks.

level_31.title: Firewall
level_31.hint: Fire burns you unless you wear fire boots. Look for the boots at the end of the corridor, then walk through the flames.

level_32.title: A Block for the Flippers
level_32.hint: Flippers let you walk through water, but a moat guards them and you have a single block. Use it on the moat: once the flippers are on your feet, no other water needs a block.

level_33.title: Slide
level_33.hint: Ice carries you until you reach solid ground, and a wall only sends you back. Slide along every corridor to collect all the chips.

level_34.title: Toboggan
level_34.hint: A bent ice tile turns your slide. Follow each track with your eyes: one ends beside the exit, so ride it last.

level_35.title: Key on the Fly
level_35.hint: A key lying on the ice is picked up as you slide over it, and a door opens as you slide into it with its key. Slide down the lane with the key to reach the door.

level_36.title: Delivery
level_36.hint: Ice carries a block the way it carries you, and a block that sinks in water leaves dirt you can walk on. Do not step on the ice yourself: you would slide into the water. Push the block into the corridor and let it slide in.

level_37.title: The Bug
level_37.hint: A bug follows the wall on its left hand and cannot cross dirt. Step on the dirt and step back: the way you open leads the bug straight into the pool.

level_38.title: Thaw
level_38.hint: A block of ice turns a fire into water, and a block of dirt fills that water. Push the ice into the flames first, then bring the dirt: the other way round, the dirt jams the fire for good.

level_39.title: Alchemy
level_39.hint: A fire takes an ice block first and a dirt block after it, a water takes a dirt block, and a block sent at the wrong hazard is lost for good. Count your blocks, and walk over the fresh dirt before the next block comes. Only one block may be in the lane at a time.

level_40.title: The Brake
level_40.hint: Ice carries you on, but a fire cell stops you if you wear the fire boots, and a water cell stops you if you wear the flippers. Wear the right boots to stop on the right cell: without them the slide ends in the flames or the water.

level_41.title: Melt and Swim
level_41.hint: A block of ice turns a fire into water, and flippers let you swim across that water: no dirt block is needed. Fetch the flippers first, cross the lake, then push the ice down its shaft and along the corridor into the flames. Pushed up against the wall, it is stuck.

level_42.title: Roller Coaster
level_42.hint: Ride the ice track in one go: its bends carry you over all five chips. The track crosses itself, and whichever end you start from, you pick them all up.
